author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed via option (a) (document the limitation prominently). The bead offered two paths — (a) document, (b) implement sort+position properly — and ranked (a) as 'minimal' for a study-impl concern. Applied (a):

  1. Added a 'Caveats' section to MemoryBackend's crate-level rustdoc (memory.rs:359-389) enumerating FOUR teach-by-bad-example shortcuts the reference impl carries: sort-not-honored, filter-coverage-narrow (only inCalendar), no-recurrence-expansion, no-availability-calculation. Each caveat cites the relevant spec section and explicitly tells production-backend implementors they MUST address it.
  2. Added a bd:JMAP-ic0j.16 reference comment at query_objects (memory.rs:847-870) pointing readers back to the Caveats section.

Did NOT pursue option (b) — implementing sort would be its own scoped epic (CalendarEventComparator property dispatch over JSON Value; canonical mail-server has a Mailbox-specific impl + Email-specific impl, each ~50 lines; calendars would need ~3-4 similar impls plus tests). That's appropriate for a production-grade follow-up, not for a P3 study-impl polish bead.

The bead's position-semantics concern (part 2) was self-resolved in the bead body ('That's actually correct... Probably fine'); no code change required.

Verified: RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc clean, clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test --all-features 120+13+1 passed.
